title: Ordinary ringed pullback agrees with completed integral pullback on constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $R=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, and $t$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of noetherian finite-dimensional schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Here noetherian means locally noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, and finite-dimensional means that lengths of strict chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets have a finite bound. No separatedness or linearity over a base field is assumed. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_W=\varprojlim_n(R/t^n)_W$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $c_f:f^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$ be the ring-sheaf map whose composite with the $n$-th projection is $c^f_{R/t^n}\circ f^{-1}(\pi_n)$, using the constant coefficient structure maps of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The categories $D(B_W)$ are the ordinary unbounded derived categories of sheaves of $B_W$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $P_f:D(B_Y)\to D(B_X)$ for ordinary ringed-topos derived pullback,
$$P_fK=B_X\otimes^L_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}K,$$
as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and $\widehat P_f$ for the completed pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

For $K\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the object $P_fK$ belongs to $D^b_c(X,R)$ and the canonical completion comparison
$$\eta_{f,K}:P_fK\longrightarrow\widehat P_fK$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K$. This is the following specified map, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of the endpoints. For a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{B_Y}(R/t^n)_Y$. The coefficient quotient maps give compatible chain maps
$$f^*_{B}Q\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_n f_n^*Q_n,$$
where $f^*_{B}Q=B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}Q$, $f_n^*$ is finite-coefficient module pullback and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ restricts the action to $B_X$. Their product is killed by $1-s$, for the actual quotient transitions. The map to the strict-tower derived-limit model $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ has these quotient maps in the unshifted product and zero in the shifted product. It represents $\eta_{f,K}$ under the K-flat and strict-tower identifications. The resulting derived map is independent of the resolution under its canonical comparison isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 (stratified perfect characterization), Lemma 6.5.9 (completed pullback), and Remark 6.8.15 (ordinary ringed coefficient functors restrict to the constructible six functors), pp. 50, 54, 62; explicit quotient-cone normalization is an agent formulation of the canonical completion map.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], $K$ has a finite stratification and pro-etale local bounded finite-projective $R$-models. Its finite-noetherian-affine-cover convention follows from local noetherianity and quasi-compactness. Apply [lem-tw-ordinary-pullback-stratified-models] to obtain the base-changed perfect models for $M=P_fK$. Apply the characterization on $X$: it explicitly identifies the category in this item, including the uniform reduction bound and compatible etale-origin witnesses. Hence $M\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and is intrinsically derived $(t)$-complete in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete].

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, both directions; base-changed perfect models supplied by the cited new lemma.

proof.text: Put $M=P_fK$ and $C_XM=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(M\otimes^L_{B_X}(R/t^n)_X)$. By [lem-pur-integral-ambient-operation-models] there is a natural isomorphism $\theta_K:C_XM\simeq\widehat P_fK$. Its strict-tower maps are the balanced associativity maps and identify the quotient augmentations, including the zero shifted-product coordinate. Hence the chain map specified in [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction] is exactly $\theta_K\operatorname{comp}_M$ on flat-term K-flat representatives. The canonical computation counit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] is invertible on these representatives. Together with the ambient lemma's compatibility with changes of representatives, this identifies the specified derived $\eta_{f,K}$, proves its naturality and proves resolution independence under the canonical comparisons.

source.place: Tags 06YY and 0G7E; canonical strict-tower augmentation comparison as stated in lem-pur-integral-ambient-operation-models, with the fixed chain map of def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction.

proof.text: The coefficient hypotheses of [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] hold for $A=R$, $I=(t)$: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives a noetherian domain with nonzero $t$, and [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] gives finite quotients and therefore additive-torsion residue. For $n\geq1$ the finite free complex $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ resolves $R/t^n$, so these quotients are perfect. Since $M$ is intrinsically complete, reconstruction makes the canonical $\operatorname{comp}_M$ invertible. The isomorphism $\theta_K$ of step 2 therefore makes the specified $\eta_{f,K}$ invertible. No separatedness or base-field linearity was used.

The ambient node, for arbitrary f with ell invertible and the same c_f and C_X, gives theta: C_X F_f K ≅ \hat F_f K. On flat-term K-flat representatives theta is built from the balanced strict-tower isomorphisms, and it identifies the quotient augmentation with the defining (a,0) augmentation. Hence eta = theta∘comp. Its compatibility with changes of representative, together with the invertible epsilon, gives naturality and independence of the resolution. Its condition (ii) matches the new node, and (ii)⇒(i) gives the item's category and Koszul derived completeness.
